domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is RAG architecture, chunking, semantic objects, multi-field search, and alternatives to vector databases for retrieval. Air France call center co-pilot and enterprise document knowledge bases ground this in enterprise operations and search & knowledge. EyeLevel describes a production RAG platform deployed at customer sites with reported accuracy results. The content assumes familiarity with RAG, vector databases, and chunking but remains accessible to practitioners. The video is a recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript with direct excerpts from the talk.

summary: Ben, co-founder of EyeLevel.ai, argues that RAG hallucinations originate primarily from RAG content ingestion problems rather than LLMs or prompts. He identifies three failure categories: improperly extracted text, information lost during chunking (surrounding context, section identity, document identity), and visual elements not extracted at all. EyeLevel spent four years building solutions into their ingestion pipeline, creating what they call semantic objects instead of using vector databases. Semantic objects preserve original chunk text alongside auto-generated metadata and two rewritten versions—one optimized for search and one for completion. Their ingestion pipeline runs a fine-tuned vision model on millions of documents to identify images, tables, and text, then processes each through dedicated multimodal pipelines. When a search query arrives, they rewrite it into a compatible format, search across the entire semantic object (original text, metadata, search version), and use a fine-tuned LLM to re-rank results. Over nine fine-tuned models operate across ingestion and search. Ben demonstrates with an Air France document figure, contrasting OCR-plus-vectorization information loss against EyeLevel's richer output. Air France uses the platform for a call center co-pilot handling hundreds of thousands of complex documents. EyeLevel claims 95%+ accuracy for customers including Air France and Dartmouth, 98% accuracy in a recent study, and outperformance of popular market solutions by up to 120%. Users can build enterprise-quality applications in minutes via no-code tools and APIs at i0.ai/x-ray.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Ben introduces himself and EyeLevel.ai, explains that RAG hallucinations typically come from RAG content quality issues rather than LLMs or prompts, and identifies three content problem categories: bad extraction, chunking context loss, and unextracted visual elements.

sections.title: EyeLevel Solution and Results
sections.summary: Ben describes EyeLevel's four-year development effort, their semantic objects approach replacing vector databases, and customer results including 95%+ accuracy for Air France and Dartmouth and 98% in a recent study outperforming market solutions by up to 120%.

sections.title: Air France Case Study and Technical Walkthrough
sections.summary: Ben demonstrates EyeLevel's ingestion pipeline using an Air France document example, showing how a fine-tuned vision model identifies elements, multimodal pipelines extract information, and semantic objects preserve context with dual rewritten text formats for search and completion.

sections.title: Search Process and Conclusion
sections.summary: Ben explains the query rewriting and multi-field search process across semantic objects with fine-tuned LLM re-ranking, notes over nine fine-tuned models in total, and invites the audience to try the platform at i0.ai/x-ray.
